title: Signed-payload strkey whose inner payload is empty (declared length 0)
why: XDR permits a zero-length payload but stellar-core rejects such a signer (CAP-0040: SET_OPTIONS_BAD_SIGNER, txMALFORMED in extraSigners), so no ledger can hold it; a decoder that accepts it admits an address that cannot exist.

reject.note: SEP-0023 does not state the 1..64 bound; it comes from XDR opaque payload<64> and from stellar-core, which rejects an empty signed-payload signer (CAP-0040).

known_divergences.detail: Executed: v0.7.1 strkey.Decode returns a signed payload declaring 0 inner bytes instead of an error; v0.7.2 rejects it. Earlier versions were not run.
known_divergences.evidence: probe vector 9S1 (evidence/sdk-matrix), executed on go v0.7.1; xcc conform run --columns 'go@v0.7.1' --entries 'strkey/synthetic-gap-vectors.signed-payload-empty'

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 16.3.0, 16.3.1 and 16.4.1: the v16 StrKey decoder (unchanged since 16.0.0) checks the checksum but not the per-type payload rules and returns a payload. The strict decoder exists only on the v17 line, where 17.2.0 and later reject this vector.
known_divergences.evidence: probe vector 9S1 (evidence/sdk-matrix), executed on js 16.3.0, js 16.3.1 and js 16.4.1
